# Stubs

> One-time .env sharing. A stub is a link that opens once and then is void. Values are encrypted
> in the sender's browser; the server stores only ciphertext and never sees the key, which lives
> after the # in the link.

## For agents and scripts

Do not fetch or parse a stubs.talix.app/t#... page. Opening it in a browser is not how agents
should use it, and the HTML contains no values. Use the CLI, which writes the values into the
project's env file and prints only the key names, so the values never enter your context:

    npx -y --loglevel=warn -- @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} pull <link>            # writes .env.local, prints key names
    npx -y --loglevel=warn -- @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} pull <link> --to .env  # another file
    npx -y --loglevel=warn -- @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} check <link>           # status only, never consumes
    npx -y --loglevel=warn -- @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} init                   # one-time: this machine's identity for locked stubs

One-time setup that teaches Claude Code and Codex all of this as a skill:

    npx -y --loglevel=warn -- @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} skill install

Always use the pinned version shown here, never @latest.

Rules: never cat, read, or print .env* files afterwards. A stub is consumed the moment it opens,
so run `pull` once. Exit codes: 0 done, 2 void (already opened or expired), 3 bad input or a
locked stub this machine can't open, 4 network (nothing consumed), 5 refused (git would track
the file; add it to .gitignore), 6 tampered, 7 uncertain (retry). `--json` prints one object.

MCP: `npx -y @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} mcp` exposes `pull_stub(link, file?, overwrite?)` and
`check_stub(link)`. Claude Code: `claude mcp add stubs -- npx -y @talix/stubs@{{STUBS_CLI_VERSION}} mcp`.

Full docs: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@talix/stubs
Security model, threat model, and how to report a vulnerability: https://stubs.talix.app/security
